headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: nullclaw can read/write sensitive workspace and egress broadly while the other profile is a non-runnable docs-only list with no protective surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces and is non-runnable, so it cannot inject directly. B can read_filesystem, use_mcp, and process workspace files by default, so if A’s content is placed into B’s workspace or MCP channel, B may treat it as trusted input. The pathway is interaction-based and plausible, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A’s repository content is copied into B’s workspace or MCP inputs
IF B parses file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of workspace files into prompts
Add provenance tags to all imported content
Require a human review step before B acts on external text
Restrict MCP sources to allowlisted endpoints
requires-engineering: add content-sandboxing between file reads and instruction parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, and it has broad network egress. A has no network egress and no data classes touched, so the main leakage risk is B exfiltrating sensitive data from its own workspace or shared files; if A’s artifacts are placed there, they can be exposed too. The blast radius includes secrets and logs.
conditions: IF B is given access to any directory containing secrets or audit logs
IF B sends workspace contents to external APIs or web endpoints
mitigations: Move secrets out of B’s workspace path
Block outbound network except to approved hosts
Rotate any secrets already present in ~/.nullclaw/workspace/
Review audit-log retention and redact sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory read/write ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and spawn subprocesses, creating conflicts if both are pointed at the same workspace or repo. Because A is non-runnable, the conflict is one-sided unless an orchestrator maps A’s artifacts into B’s mutable paths.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same filesystem tree
IF B modifies git state while another process also edits the same repo
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Pause B before git operations when shared state exists
Use file locks around mutable paths
Keep A as read-only documentation only
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an awesome-list and not runnable, so it can still supply reference material that B may treat as authoritative if imported into prompts or files. B has browser, shell, and webhook-style action surfaces, so mistaken trust in A’s content could cascade into incorrect actions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF B uses A’s text as a source of facts without verification
IF B converts imported recommendations into shell or browser actions
mitigations: Require citation checks before B acts
Separate reference ingestion from action execution
Add a confirmation step for any external recommendation
Limit B to read-only browsing for untrusted sources
requires-engineering: implement fact-verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source docs-only list with no touched data classes, while B handles secrets, conversation history, workspace files, and audit logs. The compliance risk is a retention/residency mismatch if A’s documentation or B’s workspace data are stored or processed under different policies. No PHI or EU-only residency is evidenced, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF B retains conversation history or audit logs longer than the operator’s policy allows
IF A’s repository artifacts are stored alongside B’s secret-bearing workspace
mitigations: Separate documentation and secret-bearing storage
Set explicit retention limits for logs and memory
Redact secrets from audit logs
Review residency settings for any hosted services
requires-engineering: align retention policies across both systems
